title: Lena and the Tide
premise: Yara Zhou has built a career on erasing himself, ghostwriting a rival's memoirs while nursing a secret dream of writing under his own name. When his late grandmother's orchard deed inexplicably lists both him and Odile Marchetti—the baker whose lease next door is expiring and the only person who ever saw through his invisibility—as co-owners, the two are legally bound to a piece of land neither can sell without the other. As they fight over the deed, they uncover that Yara's grandmother and Odile's mother once loved each other and were torn apart by the same town powers now circling the orchard. Yara must choose between finishing the memoir that will secure his career and exposing the truth in his own voice; he publishes under his own name, loses the ghostwriting contract, and gains the orchard, the bakery lease, and Odile.
about_author: Mara Coldharbour spent a decade as an uncredited writer for other people's lives before turning to fiction about people who refuse to be written over. She lives near a failing orchard she refuses to sell.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He finishes a chapter of rival author Devin Kessler's memoirs, reciting his creed that the heart is trainable muscle. His editor dangles a promotion contingent on discretion. Emotional beat: controlled detachment cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Line
chapters.summary: A probate letter arrives: Yara inherits his grandmother's orchard—co-owned with Odile Marchetti, a name he hasn't spoken in nine years. POV Yara. Beat: shock curdling into dread as old memories surface uninvited.

chapters.title: Flour and Thorns
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She confronts Yara at her bakery, lease expiring in ninety days, furious that the deed entangles her with the man who vanished from her life. Beat: anger masking hurt; neither will sign anything.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They draft a hostile co-ownership agreement: split proceeds, sell fast, never speak of the past. A lawyer warns the deed resists division—an old covenant clause. Beat: brittle professionalism over live wires.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Walking the overgrown rows, they find two initials carved in the same tree decades apart. Yara goes quiet in a way she remembers too well. Beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Devin pressures him for the memoir's final act—a scandalous chapter about the Marchetti family's lost land claim. Yara realizes his career is built on selling Odile's history. Beat: guilt sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her landlord reveals a buyer wants the whole block, orchard included—backed by the same development firm courting Devin's publisher. Beat: the personal feud revealed as someone else's profit margin.

chapters.title: Rain on the Deed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Storm traps them in the orchard shed; they argue until the argument becomes confession—he left because her mother called him a parasite with a pen. Beat: walls down, then hastily rebuilt.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. In a locked trunk: letters between Yara's grandmother and Odile's mother, lovers separated when the town elite seized the orchard's water rights. Beat: awe and grief; their story rhymes with the present.

chapters.title: Devin's Version
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Devin announces his memoir will 'expose' the Marchettis' fraudulent claim—using Yara's research. The promotion is the leash. Beat: complicity made unbearable.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Eviction notice posted. She considers signing the sale just to survive, hating herself. Yara appears at closing hour and stops it—not with money, but by invoking the covenant clause. Beat: first true alliance.

chapters.title: Covenant
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The clause requires both heirs to 'steward' the land jointly for one season before any sale. They're stuck together through harvest. Beat: trap becoming refuge.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working the trees side by side; the town watches, gossips, and some old neighbors bring tools and stories. Beat: belonging arriving sideways, unasked.

chapters.title: The Chapter He Can't Write
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Deadline looms; every draft of Devin's final chapter reads like betrayal. He writes instead, secretly, the true history in his own voice. Beat: the invisible man choosing visibility on paper first.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She finds his manuscript pages in the orchard office and reads all night—him, finally legible. She says nothing, waiting for him to offer it himself. Beat: love as patience.

chapters.title: Pressure Points
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Devin threatens to reveal Yara's ghostwriting to burnish his own brand unless the chapter lands. The development firm offers Odile's landlord a sweeter deal. Beat: pincers closing.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Yara confesses everything: the memoir, the threat, the manuscript. She doesn't forgive instantly; she asks what he'll do. Beat: the question that matters more than forgiveness.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He publishes the true history online under his own name hours before Devin's launch, detonating his career. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the muscle finally trained to tell the truth.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Publishing world burns; Devin retaliates; the development deal wobbles under public scrutiny of the seized water rights. Odile stands beside Yara publicly. Beat: cost counted, worth weighed.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Climax. Town council hearing on the orchard and water rights. Yara testifies with the letters; Odile speaks for the bakery and the block. The council voids the old seizure. Beat: the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: First Light, First Print
chapters.summary: Resolution begins. Yara signs a modest book deal of his own; Odile's lease converts to ownership of the bakery. They replant the carved tree's row together. Beat: quiet joy, earned.

chapters.title: Lena and the Tide
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating. Named for the grandmother who wrote the covenant's loophole, the orchard reopens as a community harvest. Yara's novel—this book—sits on the bakery counter. Final beat: the heart, trainable after all, chooses to stay.
